title: Windrow House Rising
premise: Zephyrine Whitlock, the famously discreet concierge of the Windrow House hotel, is paid a suspiciously generous retainer by a dying magnate to prove that his daughter's murder — solved and closed a decade ago — never happened. As Zephyrine peels back the official story, he finds the original verdict was purchased, not proven, and that everyone who protected it has something left to lose. The trail leads to the magnate's own household, where love against duty forced a loyal servant to bury the truth, and power corrupted everyone who touched it. In the end Zephyrine must choose between loyalty to his client and the truth: he exposes the real killer — the magnate's son, now heir — but only after the dying man signs a confession absolving the servant who helped cover it up.
about_author: Quentin Marchetti spent fifteen years working front desks in grand European hotels before turning to crime fiction, collecting the secrets guests thought no one overheard. He writes from a small apartment above a shuttered pension in Trieste, where he still answers the door for strangers.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A frail magnate, Edmund Voss, arrives at Windrow House and pays a year's fees upfront to prove his daughter Isolde's decade-old murder never happened. Zephyrine, who never takes an unclosable case, accepts against instinct. Beat: unease disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Ten Years Cold
chapters.summary: Zephyrine reviews the closed case file: Isolde Voss drowned in the hotel's own boathouse; a groundskeeper confessed and died in prison. POV shifts to a 2014 newspaper account. Beat: the neatness of the old story begins to itch.

chapters.title: The Staff Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine interviews long-serving Windrow employees, most notably housekeeper Marta Ilves, who was Isolde's confidante. Her grief is precise, rehearsed. His POV. Beat: first crack — someone here remembers differently.

chapters.title: Paid to Doubt
chapters.summary: Zephyrine wonders why a grieving father wants the murder undone rather than avenged. He digs into Voss's finances and finds hush payments made after the trial. His POV. Beat: suspicion turns inward toward the client himself.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Ledger
chapters.summary: In archived ledgers, Zephyrine finds the boathouse was locked that night — from outside. Someone with a key. Flashback chapter in Marta's POV, 2014, watching Isolde sneak out to meet a lover. Beat: dread blooming under nostalgia.

chapters.title: A Son's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Julian Voss arrives unannounced, charming and watchful, urging Zephyrine to drop the case for his father's peace of mind. Zephyrine's POV. Beat: threat wrapped in courtesy; the stakes become personal.

chapters.title: What Marta Kept
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. She reveals Isolde was pregnant and planned to run away with a lover her father forbade — but she swears she doesn't know who the lover was. A lie Zephyrine lets stand. Beat: loyalty vs. truth takes human shape.

chapters.title: The Confession That Was Bought
chapters.summary: Zephyrine traces the groundskeeper's defense lawyer: paid by Voss family counsel to steer a guilty plea. His POV, with a tense interview of the now-disgraced lawyer. Beat: the case wasn't closed; it was purchased.

chapters.title: Night Water
chapters.summary: Zephyrine searches the drained boathouse at night and finds a woman's locket wedged in the pilings — engraved with initials that aren't the groundskeeper's. His POV. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear as headlights sweep the shore.

chapters.title: The Lover's Name
chapters.summary: The initials point to Julian. Zephyrine confronts the timeline: Julian claimed to be abroad, but ferry records say otherwise. His POV. Beat: the horror of suspecting the client's own blood.

chapters.title: Dying Declarations
chapters.summary: Edmund Voss's POV. The magnate confesses his motive: not denial but inheritance — he learned the truth years ago and buried it to protect Julian, and now wants absolution before death. Beat: power's corruption laid bare; pity and revulsion entwined.

chapters.title: Silence for Sale
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks Zephyrine's office; the locket vanishes. Hotel security footage is wiped by someone with master-key access. His POV. Beat: the enemy is inside the house; paranoia tightens.

chapters.title: Marta Disappears
chapters.summary: Marta fails to appear for her shift; her room is stripped. Zephyrine realizes his questions painted a target on her. His POV, guilt-driven urgency. Beat: love against duty — his duty to truth endangers those he's come to care for.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Zephyrine obtains the 2014 ferry manifest proving Julian returned secretly the night of the murder — and that Marta saw him at the dock. His POV. Beat: the pieces lock together with terrible weight.

chapters.title: What the Groundskeeper Knew
chapters.summary: Zephyrine visits the dead man's widow, who hands over letters proving her husband saw Julian by the boathouse and was coerced into pleading guilty to spare the family name. Her POV frame within his visit. Beat: righteous anger; the cost of bought silence.

chapters.title: An Offer
chapters.summary: Julian offers Zephyrine a partnership — money, position, discretion — revealing he knows about the locket. Zephyrine stalls, buying time. His POV. Beat: temptation as menace; the corruption of power tries to recruit him.

chapters.title: Marta's Choice
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Hiding in a coastal pension, she drafts a full statement: she saw Julian that night, stayed silent because Isolde begged her to protect the unborn child's father. Beat: heartbreak — loyalty weaponized into complicity.

chapters.title: The Storm
chapters.summary: A storm strands everyone at Windrow House. Julian, cornered by Zephyrine's summons, comes for the last witness. Zephyrine's POV, racing through dark corridors. Beat: rising dread into open confrontation.

chapters.title: Boathouse Reckoning
chapters.summary: Climax. Julian corners Marta at the boathouse; Zephyrine intervenes, forcing a confession out of him as Edmund arrives, collapsing. Julian nearly kills again; police, tipped earlier by Zephyrine, arrive. Beat: violence, confession, near-tragedy.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Dying Edmund signs a sworn statement exonerating the groundskeeper and implicating Julian, then dies at dawn. Zephyrine's POV, hollowed by victory. Beat: truth won, but at a price that can't be refunded.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Julian is charged; the groundskeeper's name is cleared posthumously; Marta, freed of her secret, chooses to stay at Windrow House on her own terms. Zephyrine's POV. Beat: quiet repair; loyalty and truth finally aligned.

chapters.title: The Next Client
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A new guest leaves an envelope at the desk — another impossible request. He hesitates, glances at the lake, and this time reads the terms twice before accepting. Beat: wry closure; the watcher remains watched.
